Quick drafts below (happy to refine):

2) Tenant isolation (Draft):
Redwood Inference provides logical tenant isolation at the application and storage layers for our Hosted API offering. Customer data (metadata, usage logs, and KV cache snapshots) are logically partitioned by customer ID; strong RBAC and encryption-at-rest ensure isolation. For Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity), customers receive isolated GPU pools and optional VPC peering; control-plane services remain logically separated, and network isolation is enforced via customer-dedicated subnets and security group policies. (See attached: tenant_isolation_diagram.png — high level)

4) SSO & provisioning (Draft):
We support SAML 2.0 for SSO with metadata exchange and SCIM 2.0 for automated user provisioning. Common IdPs supported: Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace. Sample SAML metadata and SCIM endpoint pattern attached as scim-example.txt and saml-metadata-example.xml.

3) Data residency (Draft):
Customers can select region-scoped retention for persisted logs and long-term artifacts in Redwood Private and Dedicated offerings. For Hosted customers, we currently support US and EU retention regions; a plan for APAC region availability is scheduled for H2 2026. Please note that some ephemeral runtime telemetry used for autoscaling may be aggregated cross-region for resilience; persisted artifacts are kept within the selected region.

Attachments referenced: tenant_isolation_diagram.png, scim-example.txt, saml-metadata-example.xml

If you want me to tighten wording for legal review, say so and I'll convert to contract-friendly phrasing.

— Karthik
